chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: The five-piece band that played for Mexican dances
summary: Spikes goes through a photograph of the small band with Leon White, Bill Perkins, Eugene Wright and Massengail that played the Mexican dances twice a week.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was in the band with you during those years?
You got the picture of the band there...uh...
That the picture of the recording band? That picture? That's later, isn't it?
No, the other one on there. You got a picture
of two bands there, ain't you? Yeah. There's the recording band. That's late '20s, right?
That wasn't a picture that we played for the Mexicans all around... The other picture. You know, the picture that's in the book [Albert McCarthy: Big Band Jazz]
That's Reb's American Legion Club Band.

This little one down here. That's the one. 'Course, we never... We added a tuba player after we got another job but we only had about five who played for the Mexicans--the piano player...and the piano player. He's the piano player... the piano player and the trombone player and the banjo player and the trumpet player and the drummer. That's about all we had--about five or six places--for the Mexican...uh...dances.
So that's Leon White, trombone, and Bill Perkins, guitar, and Eugene Wright on piano and you on saxophone and...uh, probably a drummer but...
Because here it says "unknown." I guess they didn't know the name of the drummer in the picture here.
Well, it wouldn't make any difference, but

anyway, that's what we...we used to play mostly for the Mexicans--about five pieces, you know, and at least two nights a week, and they wanted jazz, you know. 'Course, Gene was a great piano player, and so was Massengail on the trumpet, you know, and they liked all that stuff.
